observations: 1078 HTTP observations logged (10 warmup + 240 LOCALHOST + 240 DYNAMIC + 240 HIT-POPULATE + 240 HIT + 18 STABILITY + 15 HIT-IDENTITY + 45 HIT-DEPTH + 30 HIT-LARGE); zero transport errors; zero duplicate (session_kind, cell, rep) keys.

Phase 0 infrastructure: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) with proxy_cache; warm-up of 10 consecutive GETs to one fixed URL produced X-Cache MISS,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT,HIT (9/10 HIT; first request is the cache populate).
DYNAMIC path: 240/240 responses carried X-Cache: MISS (unique cache-busting query per request; cache key is $request_uri) - confirms the cache is actually engaged and keyed by URI only.

Primary HIT path: populate+test, 48 cells x 5 reps with 1-3s delay between populate and test; 240/240 test-phase responses carried X-Cache: HIT; 48 populate responses were MISS (first populate of each cell), 192 were HIT (subsequent populate requests).
Oracle-free greedy decode (try brotli then gzip iteratively, MAX_DEPTH=5, no SHA256 oracle) produced byte-identical output to ground truth for 1078/1078 observations (every session kind).
C8 identity: for all 48 primary cells the DYNAMIC-path wire bytes and HIT-path wire bytes are identical (body sha256, base64, Content-Encoding, Content-Length). Cache HIT serving did not alter bytes.
Cache stability: 6/6 groups (2 JSON, 2 HTML, 1 BINARY, 1 large JSON) byte-stable over 3 consecutive requests 1s apart; X-Cache sequence MISS,HIT,HIT in each group.
Depth generalization: 45/45 observations (depth 3,4,5 x JSON/HTML/BINARY x 5 reps) decoded correctly; all served cached (36 HIT test observations after 9 first-population requests).
Large payloads: 30/30 observations (3 types x 2 orders x 5 reps, target 150000 bytes) decoded correctly; 24 HIT + 6 first-population requests.
Identity payloads: 15/15 served through cache decoded correctly (12 HIT + 3 first-population requests).
Regression baselines on the same 480 wire-byte observations (DYNAMIC+HIT): oracle-guided decode 480/480; fixed-origin-order decode 480/480 (local nginx does not transform bytes).
Zero ambiguous tie-breaks were observed in any of the 1078 rows (brotli and gzip decodes never both succeeded at the same iteration).
Ground-truth check: for all 72 registered payloads, fullbody_decompress(compressed) == plain body (gt_is_plain true); payload entropies range 4.66-7.70 bits/byte.
validity_notes: Substrate: local nginx 1.24.0 (Ubuntu) as a caching reverse proxy (proxy_cache, keys_zone spider:16m, proxy_cache_key $request_uri, proxy_cache_valid 200 5m) in front of a local Python origin (Cache-Control: public, max-age=300), HTTP/1.1, no TLS. This intentionally isolates the caching layer from CDN edge transformations; it does NOT reproduce Cloudflare's re-encoding behavior.

M-HIT-RATE 0.9455 (312/330) counts all cached-path test observations; the 18 non-HIT rows are the first (populate) request of depth/large/identity fixed URLs where the resource was not yet cached. Among responses to an already-cached resource (x-cache==HIT) accuracy and byte-identity are 312/312 = 1.0.
Depth/large/identity phases used one request per rep on a fixed URL (populate then HIT), i.e., populated-cache serves, not fresh-cache first requests; all decode-correct either way.

No byte transformation by nginx was observed (C8 identity 48/48 and fixed-order baseline 480/480), so claims about real CDN serving (e.g., Cloudflare re-encoding on cache serve) must NOT be extrapolated from this experiment; the parent's Cloudflare findings remain the only evidence for edge transformation.
Raw response body base64 is retained for every row in raw_cell_results.jsonl, allowing independent recomputation of all derived measurements; no representation loss.
Timeout/transport robustness: all 1078 requests completed with status 200; no retries required.

The claim ceiling of this run is oracle-free greedy decode accuracy on nginx-cached responses from a byte-preserving local proxy; Cloudflare free-tier,DYNAMIC-only, 0%-HIT-rate ceiling from the parent remains unmodified.
unresolved: Whether real CDN edge caches (Cloudflare etc.) alter cached-response wire bytes vs their DYNAMIC-path bytes (parent could not observe HIT responses on Cloudflare free tier; local nginx shows byte-identity, so the CDN-transformation hypothesis is untested here, only nginx-cache behavior is).
Whether oracle-free greedy decode generalizes to real-world CDN cached payloads whose framing differs from origin layering (requires an actual CDN HIT observation)
Fixed-order decode behavior on a byte-transforming CDN (parent: 60/240) versus byte-preserving proxy (here: 480/480) - the discriminator is the CDN edge, not the caching layer.
Cache freshness edge cases (expiry, revalidation, 304/REVALIDATED states) were not exercised; all serves were within the 300s max-age window.
